Build a peak catalog from a peak_params object

Source: R/peak_catalog.R
build_peak_catalog.Rd

Greedy clustering: peaks are sorted by intensity descending, each unassigned peak becomes a new cluster seed, and all remaining unassigned peaks within (eps_rt, eps_cv) of the seed are added to that cluster. Clusters are then classified into three groups:

compounds

clusters with >= min_cluster_size observations AND spanning >= min_support_frac of samples. These are the "reliable positions" the catalog is built around.

small_clusters

clusters with >= 2 observations but below the sample-support threshold. Might be sporadic contamination, small compounds, or peaks from just a few subjects.

singletons

clusters of size 1 — peaks that didn't co-locate with any other pool peak. Often noise, but worth inspecting.

Usage

build_peak_catalog(
  peak_params,
  eps_rt = 0.01,
  eps_cv = 0.05,
  min_support_frac = 0.1,
  min_cluster_size = 2L,
  coord_mode = c("fraction", "physical"),
  align = FALSE
)

Arguments

peak_params

Output of estimate_peak_params() containing rt_loc_raw, cv_loc_raw, sigma_rt_raw, sigma_cv_raw, intensity_raw, sample_idx_raw, and n_samples.

eps_rt, eps_cv

Clustering radius in fraction-of-image units. Defaults (0.01, 0.05) roughly match the peak-detector's min_sep_rt = 8, min_sep_cv = 2 on a 1400 x 40 native image. Tighter → more, smaller clusters. Looser → fewer, larger clusters. In coord_mode = "physical" they are in seconds and volts.

min_support_frac

Fraction of samples a cluster must span to count as a compound. Default 0.10: appear in at least 10% of samples.

min_cluster_size

Minimum number of pool peaks in a cluster for compound status. Default 2L (excludes singletons from compounds regardless of support).

coord_mode

"fraction" (default) clusters on rt_loc_raw / cv_loc_raw; "physical" clusters on rt_seconds_raw / cv_volts_raw (requires estimate_peak_params() to have been given time_axes / cv_axes). Either way the catalog stores fraction positions (rt_frac, cv_frac, *_frac_obs) and, when available, physical ones (rt_seconds, cv_volts, rt_seconds_obs, cv_volts_obs), all from the same member peaks.

align

Optional per-sample drift correction applied to peak_params before clustering. FALSE (default) skips alignment. TRUE calls align_via_catalog() with sensible defaults (eps_rt_loose = 3 * eps_rt, eps_cv_loose = 3 * eps_cv, min_support_frac = min_support_frac, iterate = TRUE, max_iter = 3L). Pass a named list to override any of those. Alignment is idempotent and safe to leave off if drift is small; see the compactness-delta table in compare_all_catalogs.Rmd for how to decide whether it helps on your cohort.

Value

An object of class peak_catalog with fields:

compounds

tibble of compound entries — one row per compound with columns compound_id, rt_loc, cv_loc, location_sd_rt, location_sd_cv, n_observations, n_samples, prevalence, and list-columns sigma_rt_obs, sigma_cv_obs, intensity_obs, rt_frac_obs, cv_frac_obs, member_indices, plus rt_seconds_obs, cv_volts_obs when physical positions exist and sample_idx_obs (source sample of each observation) when data dims are known.

small_clusters

same schema, for clusters below thresholds.

singletons

same schema, for clusters of size 1.

parameters

the settings used to build the catalog, plus data_dims: the n_samples x 2 matrix of each sample's unpadded rows, cols (from peak_params$data_dims, or the axis lengths in time_ranges / cv_ranges), which generators use to place observations on a centre-padded canvas (catalog_pixel_positions()); and grid, the dms_grid() the samples were resampled onto (if recorded), through which generators map rt_seconds_obs / cv_volts_obs to pixels.

Details

Uses a sorted-index optimization so runtime stays O(n log n + n·k) rather than O(n^2), where k is the average number of candidates per seed. Practical for pool sizes up to millions.
